Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a markedly smaller and hyperlucent right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings, indicative of oligemia. In the context of Takayasu arteritis, which causes large vessel vasculitis, this appearance is characteristic of chronic obstruction or stenosis of the right pulmonary artery leading to hypoplasia and reduced blood flow to the affected lung.
